newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian opposition asks for vote postponement.
newsitem.headline: Croatian opposition asks for vote postponement.

text.p: Croatia's opposition Social Liberal party called on Tuesday for Sunday's presidential election to be postponed by two weeks after its candidate Vlado Gotovac was attacked at a campaign rally.

"The reason for this is the attempt on the life of Vlado Gotovac in Pula that happened on the fifth of this month, when he sustained such injuries that he was thrown out of the presidential race," party secretary Karl Gorinsek told a news conference.

Gotovac suffered concussion and neck injuries after being hit on the head with a belt buckle last week. He fell to the ground and was treated in hospital. Doctors said on Monday he had to refrain from any activity and stay in bed.

The party asked for both other candidates, President Franjo Tudjman and Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democratic party, to stop campaigning until Gotovac is better. They also said Gotovac should be allowed to add on the days he has lost to lengthen his campaign.
The Liberal party said if their demand was not met Gotovac would still stand as a candidate in Sunday's vote and rumours of him withdrawing were absolutely false, Gorinsek said.
Gotovac and Tomac are fighting a losing battle to try and oust Tudjman, who is widely expected to win the election in the first round.
